newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN AND CO. BEAT HEAT TO REACH FINALS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN AND CO. BEAT HEAT TO REACH FINALS.

text.p: Michael Jordan scored 15 of his 28 points in the first quarter as the defending champion Chicago Bulls returned to the NBA Finals with an easy 100-87 victory over the Miami Heat on Wednesday.

The Bulls eliminated the feisty but undermanned Heat in five games in the Eastern Conference finals and await the winner of the Western Conference series between the Utah Jazz and the Houston Rockets. They reached the NBA Finals for the fifth time in seven years, also winning titles in 1991, 1992 and 1993.
After failing to sweep the Heat in Game Four in Miami, the Bulls returned home and quickly took control.
They never trailed, scoring the first eight points and opening a 33-19 lead after one quarter. The Heat never got within single digits thereafter.

Chicago won without any contribution from Scottie Pippen, who suffered a sprained left foot midway through the first quarter and did not return. Luc Longley and Ron Harper picked up the slack with 14 points apiece.

Pippen still had the knot on his head from an elbow from Alonzo Mourning in Miami's Game Four win. Jordan did not take kindly to that and refused to shake hands with Mourning in the pre-game meeting with the referees.
"They came in and beat us up pretty bad," Jordan said on Wednesday, referring to Game Four.

Jordan said that on Wednesday, "we were back in our own home court and we wanted to make a stand. We didn't want to beat them up, we wanted to beat them on the court. It was about intensity in the game.
"It wasn't to go out there and fight, throw elbows whatever, not as physical to where it ends up fighting. We weren't going to let them come in and push us around," Jordan said.
Jordan set the tone for the game in the first quarter, shaking off a 9-for-35 performance in Game Four.
Mourning, who guaranteed a win in Game Four, was held without a field goal until making a three-pointer in the final seconds. He scored 13 points.

Tim Hardaway had 27 points and Jamal Mashburn added 22 for the Heat, who saw the most successful campaign in franchise history come to an end. Miami, which won 61 games this season, had never won a playoff series prior to this year.

Miami coach Pat Riley said, "we sensed impending doom coming here, but we wanted to play with intensity and get ahead early. They took that away right away with a 16-3 run and we never really got close."

Jordan, who missed his first 14 shots Monday, made two jumpers in the 8-0 burst that opened the game. He added two free throws and a jumper before Longley made a hook to extend the advantage to 16-2 with 7:01 left in the period.
Chicago coach Phil Jackson said, "I hope the Houston-Utah series goes seven games. Jordan shot better but not as well as usual (11-35). A few days off before the finals will help us."

Before Pippen departed, he made two foul shots that gave the Bulls an 18-7 lead with 5:30 left. The lead never dipped below 10 points after that. Chicago shot 63 percent (12-of-19) in the first quarter and held Miami to 29 percent (6-of-21). Jordan made 6-of-10 shots.
Miami shot just 36 percent (26-of-72), including 10-of-30 from behind the arc.

Miami closed to 40-30 on two free throws by Mashburn with 7:35 to go in the second quarter, but Chicago responded with a 12-4 run, opening its largest lead at 52-34 on a dunk by Randy Brown with 4:30 left.

The Heat rebounded with a 12-4 run of their own, again closing to 10 points at 56-46 with 2:33 remaining. But Jordan made a free throw and Steve Kerr drilled a three-pointer, helping the Bulls open a 64-50 halftime lead.
It was the best first half of the playoffs for Chicago, which was limited to a playoff-worst 31 points in the first half of Game Four.

Longley scored five points in a lackluster third quarter that saw the Bulls take an 80-65 advantage into the final period. A three-point play by Mashburn cut the deficit to 88-78 with 5:35 to play, but Harper made a three-pointer and Jordan hit a pair of free throws.

Jordan and Mourning received double technicals with 2:38 left. Bulls forward Dennis Rodman, who had nine points, 13 rebounds and four assists, was whistled for taunting midway through the third period and has received a technical foul in each playoff game.
Brian Williams scored 10 points for Chicago, which shot 46 percent (39-of-84) and held a 53-36 rebounding edge. Jordan cooled off after his hot start and finished 11-of-31.
